headline: Heath Moss favours Bellevue Gold as hedging rolls off and debt is paid down, setting up FY27 as a re-rating catalyst
reasoning: Bellevue Gold has underperformed gold peers recently because it carries debt and a hedge book with prices locked in around A$3,000/oz against a current spot price above A$6,000/oz, creating a significant opportunity cost. However, moving into FY27 they have no hedging to deliver until Q4 and even then only 68,000oz is in question. Production is running at approximately 40,000oz per quarter, implying roughly 160,000oz in FY27 rising to 180,000oz beyond that. As the hedge book unwinds, the company gains much greater exposure to the prevailing gold price, generating higher free cash flow to pay down debt. Heath expects the market to re-rate the stock as investors gain confidence in production targets being met and the balance sheet improving.
quote: Bellevue Gold BGO. Um, been held back and hasn't been performed as well as some of the other Goldie's in the last couple of weeks, and that's simply because it carries a bit of debt and it's hedge, but it's still got a bit of a hedge book there, which, um, prices are hedged around $3,000, uh, Australian. And when you consider the current prices, you know, over $6,000 Australian, they're losing out quite a bit there. But moving forward into full year 27, they don't have any hedging to deliver until the fourth quarter. If they choose to do so, that's only 68,000, um, uh, ounces. They're producing about 40,000oz, uh, a quarter. So they're looking at around 160,000 for full year 27 and then 180,000 beyond that. So the story moving forward is a the market gaining confidence in them and getting be able to hit those production uh targets had a hedging coming off the debt being paid down because they'll get more free cash flow because they're getting more exposure to that higher gold price. So I really like them here as well.
